## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 89 (*Vāsitaka*, "Bathing with sesame paste") is a vinaya rule for Buddhist nuns (*bhikkhunī*s) in the Pali Vinaya Piṭaka [SuttaCentral]. The rule establishes that a nun incurs an offense requiring confession (*pācittiya*) if she bathes with scents and oil-seed flowers or scented sesame paste [SuttaCentral]. An English translation of the text has been made available by Bhikkhu Brahmali on SuttaCentral [SuttaCentral]. While the secondary literature search gathered several references to "Pācittiya 89", all pertain to the monk's rule (*Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga*) concerning borderless sitting mats rather than this nun's rule.

SuttaCentral notes wide-ranging parallels to this rule across early monastic traditions [SuttaCentral]. Within the Pali canon, it corresponds to Bhikkhunī Pātimokkha Pācittiya 89 and Bhikkhunī Parivāra Pācittiya 89, closely following the preceding rule on bathing with scented clay or powders (*Gandhavaṇṇaka*, Bi-Vb Pc88) [SuttaCentral]. Parallels and resembling regulations exist in the vinayas of the Dharmaguptaka (Chinese Vibhaṅga Pc 151), Mahīśāsaka (Chinese Vibhaṅga Pc 154), Mūlasarvāstivāda (Tibetan Vinaya Pc 120 and Chinese Vibhaṅga Pc 167/168), Sarvāstivāda (Sanskrit fragment and Chinese Vibhaṅga Pc 164), and Mahāsāṅghika-Lokottaravāda (Sanskrit and Chinese Vibhaṅga Pc 126) [SuttaCentral]. Machine text-reuse analysis via DharmaNexus shows extensive phraseological overlap within the Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga itself, sharing its largest internal match with Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 88 (§0.1–2.2.5 ↔ §0.1–2.2.4; 2,392 matching characters), along with substantial parallels in Pācittiya 87 and Nissaggiya Pācittiya 6 [DharmaNexus]. DharmaNexus also records cross-linguistic alignment with the Tibetan Vinaya (BO_K01_D0003-3_H0003-3) [DharmaNexus].

*No discussion of this text was found in the reference-literature corpus; the overview relies on SuttaCentral and DharmaNexus data.*
